 Advertisement Longtime WCVB-TV news anchor, reporter Jim Boyd dies
 Advertisement Updated: 8:42 PM EDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Longtime WCVB-TV news anchor, reporter Jim Boyd dies
 Updated: 8:42 PM EDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ BOSTON — Jim Boyd, former anchor and reporter at WCVB-TV for nearly four decades, has died. Boyd was 84 years old. 
 Boyd began his career in public television in the mailroom of WNET-TV, New York in 1961. He moved on to roles in public affairs and production before joining the staff of WGBH-TV’s "Say Brother." 
 Advertisement Boyd then returned to WNET-TV as an associate producer and then producer of the Emmy Award-winning program "News in Perspective." 
 For a guy who enjoyed tremendous success in his career, Jim Boyd says he was never successful as a student in New York City's Harlem.
 “I liked to play. I liked to play sports. I liked to pretty much do anything other than go to school and sit in class and come home and do homework. I just never really got into school as something that I was enthusiastic about. Never really enjoyed it and never was very successful.”
 Watch below: Maria Stephanos and Jorge Quiroga remember Jim Boyd 
 After struggling through high school, Jim did manage to get into college, but called that experience a disaster.
 “I was academically dismissed from Long Island University in 1961. And the one thing that I didn't know is that it was too much of a burden and too much of a sacrifice of my parents for me to just blow it entirely. I went out to find a job. There wasn't much that was available to me. So I started working in the mailroom in a non-commercial television. The more I learned about the organization, the more I learned about the industry, the more I learned about you know, the writing part and the news part, you know, the more enthusiastic I got. So finally, I got enthusiastic about something.”
 Jim worked his way up from the mailroom to production assistant to producer and eventually landed here at WCVB-TV as a reporter in 1972.
 He began as a general assignment reporter and eventually moved to anchoring the weekend and EyeOpener newscasts and was co-anchor of the Midday newscast with Susan Wornick. 
 Hearst Owned Susan Wornick and Jim Boyd After he retired in 2008, Boyd received a bachelor's degree in sociology from Tufts University in 2013.
 "I struggle with trying to find the adequate words to explain just how great it felt to be able to get that degree and walk across that stage," Boyd said in an interview with "Chronicle."
 Boyd received the Golden Circle award from the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences New England chapter in 2011 and was inducted into the Massachusetts Broadcasters Hall of Fame in 2012.
 In 2022, Boyd and Wornick made a surprise appearance during WCVB-TV's 50 Years Fund telethon.
 Boyd was an active member of the community, working with several youth organizations.
 Boyd is survived by Linda, his wife of 42 years, and three daughters.
